correctness.rationale: For a multiple N of b^r+1 with digit sum <=b, regroup digits by exponents modulo 2r into signed coefficients c_i with L1 norm <=b. A coefficient of absolute value b makes the nonzero relation magnitude b^(i+1)<b^r+1. Otherwise every coefficient magnitude <=b-1, and absolute sum <b^r+1, forcing integer relation zero. Uniqueness of signed base-b coefficients in (-b,b) forces all c_i=0; total digit sum must then be even. The modulus itself has digit sum 2, and 1+sum_(j=0)^(b-1) b^(r-1+2rj) has digit sum b+1 and is divisible by the modulus. Carry-free concatenation of positive multiples realizes every positive combination of these generators. For even b the generated semigroup is precisely evens >=2 and odds >=b+1; no other small odds occur. Python finite automaton checks 35 parameter pairs and direct exact witness arithmetic 325 settings/sums, independent of the general proof.

value.rationale: The 2023 study explicitly asks in Question 4 for exact Frobenius numbers of digit-sum output sets in the coprime regime. Here an entire natural two-parameter family of shifted powers b^r+1 is classified completely, with exact omitted positive sums, conductor b, Frobenius number b-1 and b/2 gaps independent of r. The signed short-relation lemma gives a structural mechanism for the unexpectedly stable gaps beyond mere arithmetic-progression attainability. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice or table recomputation.
